hits.text:
Sometimes social trends gain steam, but if you're a serious person you just analyze them individually and swat them down if they're not good.

I invite you to watch this chat on algos and your free will.

The interviewer was weak but the guest was great.

hits.hook: Sometimes social trends gain steam, but if you're a serious person you just analyze them individually and swat them down if they're not good.
hits.draft_en:
Narratives gain steam. Data doesn't care.

My filter for any $BTC narrative:
- what number would prove it?
- has it happened before?
- what's the base rate?

If it can't answer those, it's a vibe.

Save this / follow for the filter.
hits.draft_quote_en: Same applies to markets: every narrative should be judged on its own data, not on how loud it got.
hits.video_tip: Trend arrow going up, then a filter funnel with 3 questions; 7s.
hits.reply_angle: Bridge to markets: judge each narrative by the data that would prove it, not by its momentum.
hits.why_chosen: Off-lane post but its idea (judge trends individually) bridges to evaluating crypto narratives.

hits.name: DocumentingBTC
hits.text: Why Quantum Computers Can Never Break Bitcoin https://t.co/NEaqnRDMsD
hits.hook: Why Quantum Computers Can Never Break Bitcoin https://t.co/NEaqnRDMsD
hits.draft_en:
"Quantum can never break Bitcoin" and "quantum will kill Bitcoin" are both too confident.

What's real:
- exposed public keys are the risk surface
- Bitcoin can upgrade signatures
- timing is the unknown

I don't price a date nobody knows. I watch for the upgrade path.

Save this / repost for the next quantum panic.
hits.draft_quote_en: "Never" is a strong word. Exposed public keys are a real surface; the question is whether the upgrade happens before the hardware does.
hits.video_tip: 'NEVER' in big text, strike-through, replaced by 'upgrade path'; 6s.
hits.reply_angle: Push on 'never': exposed-pubkey coins are the real risk; ask what the migration plan and timeline look like.
hits.why_chosen: Strong bold title (2.2K engagements) on quantum: room for a nuanced 'never is a strong word' reply.

viral.why_it_worked: Absolute, reassuring title on a fear topic: identity (holders want reassurance) and video format; strong share psychology.
hook_options: Quantum won't kill Bitcoin. But 'never' is wrong too.
The quantum debate has two wrong sides.
Which coins are actually exposed to quantum? Not all of them.
Fear says 'soon'. Hype says 'never'. Both skip the upgrade.
viral.optimized_version:
The quantum debate has two wrong sides.

'Never' ignores coins with exposed public keys.
'Soon' ignores that Bitcoin can migrate signatures.

What I watch instead:
- share of coins with exposed keys (check on-chain studies)
- progress on post-quantum proposals

Is your stack in an address that has never spent?

hits.name: APompliano
hits.text: I don't think most people realize how much money the government is going to print in the next decade.
hits.hook: I don't think most people realize how much money the government is going to print in the next decade.
hits.draft_en:
"The government will print a lot" is a vibe. M2 is a number.

Before you size a $BTC position on a debasement thesis:
- check M2 growth vs. $BTC returns by cycle
- check how long the lag was
- check the drawdowns in between

Thesis without a timeline is a hope.

Save this / follow for the backtest.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Probably true. But how much, and over what lag?

If $BTC is a liquidity trade, the M2 curve should tell us when, not just if. Most people skip that part.
hits.video_tip: Printer meme, then M2 line vs $BTC log chart, caption 'if, not when'; 8s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Ask for the measurable version: which money supply series, and what lag to $BTC price would confirm it? Check M2 vs BTC by cycle.
hits.why_chosen: One-line macro claim, 109 replies, no number: room to add what 'print' means in data.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: gráfico de líneas + M2 global vs $BTC en escala log por ciclo, sin cifras inventadas (check M2 data source).

viral.why_it_worked: Contrarian 'most people don't realize' hook, one sentence, identity/status share (I'm the one who sees it), invites everyone to agree or argue; no number so replies fill the gap.
hook_options: Everyone says the printer will save $BTC. Nobody says when.
Debasement is a thesis. Lag is the trade.
I checked how $BTC behaves after money supply jumps. The timing matters more than the story.
"They'll print" is not a position size.
viral.optimized_version:
Everyone says the printer will save $BTC. Nobody says when.

What I'd actually check:
- global M2 growth by year

hits.name: BitcoinArchive
hits.text:
Binance sees $3.64B in net withdrawals in 9 hours — roughly 2.1% of total assets.

Exchange response: "Market conditions are stable." https://t.co/2OlUnJTD5o
hits.hook: Binance sees $3.64B in net withdrawals in 9 hours — roughly 2.1% of total assets.
hits.draft_en:
$3.64B left Binance in 9 hours. Reported later: ~$6.1B net in 24h.

What this is: people moving coins.
What it isn't: proof of insolvency.

What I'd watch:
- does the outflow keep going after the first wave
- do coins land in self-custody or other exchanges

Either way: your keys are the only stable condition.

Save this for the next exchange scare.
hits.draft_quote_en:
2.1% of assets in 9 hours is a number. "Market conditions are stable" is a statement.

The useful check: did the outflow slow after day one, or keep going? That separates a scare from a run.
hits.video_tip: Counter ticking up to $3.64B over 9h, then 'stable?' stamp; 7s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Separate fact from claim: outflow is data, 'stable' is a statement; ask whether day-2 flows slowed (check on-chain exchange balance).
hits.why_chosen: Hard number (3.64B in 9h, 2.1% of assets) plus an exchange quote: perfect for a fact vs. interpretation reply.
hits.story: Binance net outflows after the $6.3B hack
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: barras + salidas netas de Binance por día tras el hack (check DefiLlama), logo $BTC blanco sobre azul marino.

viral.why_it_worked: Big specific number + short timeframe + an ironic official quote; surprise and usefulness (people share to warn others).
hook_options: $3.64B walked out of Binance in 9 hours.
An exchange says 'stable'. The flows say something else.
2.1% of assets in 9 hours. Is that a run or a reflex?
The one chart to check before trusting any exchange statement.
viral.optimized_version:
$3.64B walked out of Binance in 9 hours (reported).

Fact: coins moved.
Interpretation: we don't know yet if it's a run.

The test is day 2 and day 3:
- outflows slowing = scare
- outflows steady = trust problem

Where did yours go: cold wallet or another exchange?
Save this / follow for the follow-up data.
viral.visual_or_number: Key number: $3.64B in 9h / 2.1% of assets, as reported by BitcoinArchive; verify with DefiLlama daily net flows.

hits.draft_en:
A thesis with an invalidation level is rare. Alex Thorn's: 50-week MA, ~$76K (reported).

- a plan for 'below without recovery'
- position size set before, not after

Good that someone names an invalidation level.

Open question: how many weekly closes below the 50w count as 'without recovery'? One? Three? That definition is the whole trade.
hits.reply_angle: Ask for the definition: how many weekly closes below the 50w MA invalidate it? Suggest backtesting past 50w breaks.
hits.why_chosen: Concrete invalidation level (50-week MA ~ $76K): ideal for a rules-based spot reply.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: gráfico + $BTC semanal con media de 50 semanas y rupturas previas marcadas (check data).

viral.why_it_worked: Specific level and a named analyst's falsifiable claim; usefulness (people save levels) and conversation (agree/disagree).
hook_options: Most $BTC theses can't be wrong. This one can.

hits.draft_en:

hits.why_chosen: List-format macro thesis with debatable bullets (AI, debt, socialism): room to separate fact vs opinion.
